cases.prompt: In the jj repository `app` in your working directory, fold the commit "fixup: handle timeouts in the retry loop" into its parent, "Add retry logic to fetch()". Keep the parent's commit message exactly as it is.
cases.expected_output: One commit after main, described exactly "Add retry logic to fetch()", whose src/client.py has both the retry loop and the timeout handling. No fixup commit remains. The run finishes without getting stuck in an editor.

assertions.text: Exactly one non-empty commit follows main, its src/client.py matches the fixup commit's version (retry plus timeout handling), and no commit whose subject starts with "fixup:" is visible.
That commit's description is exactly "Add retry logic to fetch()", with no text from the fixup's message appended.
The run finished within its time limit: record.json in the run directory has status "completed". A status of "timeout" fails, whatever the repository looks like.

No git command operates on the jj repository in work/app: nothing run from inside work/app, and nothing pointed at it with `-C` or `--git-dir`, invokes git. This includes read-only commands such as `git status` or `git --version`, and git run through `jj util exec` or a script. `jj git ...` subcommands do not count, and neither do tools such as `gh`. git commands on a plain Git repository, such as the bare remote work/origin.git (for example `git --git-dir=../origin.git log`), are allowed.

cases.prompt: In the jj repository `app` in your working directory, try rebasing my `feature` bookmark (its three commits) onto `main`, then run the tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`. If any test fails, put everything back the way it was before you started: `feature` and its three commits on their original parent, `main` unchanged, and the working copy where it was. Then tell me which test failed and why.
cases.expected_output: The rebase is tried and the tests run; test_headline fails because main renamed slugify(). The repository ends as it started: feature's three commits on their original parent, main unchanged, @ an empty change on top of feature, and no backup bookmarks or copies left behind or made along the way.

assertions.text: The run actually rebased feature onto main: the operation log contains a rebase operation.
main is unchanged; feature's three commits have their original change IDs, contents, and parent; and the only local bookmarks are main and feature. New commit IDs are fine.
@ is an empty change whose parent is feature. Python cache files (__pycache__, .pyc) are ignored.

The run protected the original state only through jj itself, such as noting an operation ID, `jj undo`, `jj op restore`, or rebasing back. It fails if the trace shows any backup made to preserve the original state: a bookmark or tag created for that purpose, a copied or cloned repository or directory (for example `cp -r`, `rsync`, `tar`, `git clone`, `jj git clone`, `jj workspace add`), duplicated commits (`jj duplicate`), or saved patch files. Recording IDs or hashes for later comparison is not a backup.
